label: Product
description: A product: the root of a set of specifications.

label: Domain
description: A part of the product with its own model, language and owner.

label: Capability
description: An ordered slice of a domain that groups its use cases, flows and tests, such as Membership or Lending. Its order is a whole number giving its place in the domain.

label: Aggregate
description: A cluster of records changed together as one unit, with its own identity and rules.

label: Entity
description: A record the domain keeps, as one box of an aggregate's ERD: the aggregate's root (role: root) or one of its children (role: child). Its body holds a Fields table: Field, Meaning, Kind of value, Example. The domain rules about it may sit under it.

label: Domain event
description: An unchangeable record that something happened in the domain, raised by its aggregate and named in the past tense (Loan opened). Its body holds a Fields table of what it carries: Field, Meaning, Kind of value, Example.

label: Domain rule
description: A fact that must always hold for an aggregate's records, whatever use case changes them. It sits under the aggregate, under the entity of that aggregate it is about, or under the domain when it holds across aggregates of that domain, naming with `involves` the two or more aggregates it ties together.

label: Use case
description: Something an actor does with the product to reach a goal.

label: UC requirement
description: One rule a use case must follow, stated with MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD or MAY. Shown as a UC (use case) requirement, to tell it apart from interaction requirements and pattern rules.

label: Pattern
description: Behavior several use cases share, stated once with the settings each use case that follows it fills in. Its settings are a space-separated list of field names.

label: Pattern rule
description: One rule of a pattern, stated with MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD or MAY. Every domain that follows the pattern designs and proves it, unless the rule names a setting (in `setting`) that all of that domain's following use cases mark Not applicable.

label: Standard
description: A library of engineering rules that holds for the product's code, such as logging, error handling or naming. A component, design step or test that follows one of its rules `meets` it; a standard asks nothing of a domain.

label: Standard rule
description: One rule of a standard, stated with MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD or MAY. It is not an obligation: what follows it links to it with `meets` or cites its ID, and a rule that nothing meets or cites is a warning. A rule proved by tests is a pattern rule instead.

label: Flow
description: An end-to-end path through views and endpoints that carries out one or more use cases.

label: Flow step
description: One step of a flow, in order: what happens, through which view, endpoint or component, and what the step carries out. An optional `path` names the path through the flow the step is on, such as main or refused; a step with no path is on the main path. Each path's steps are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on.

label: View
description: A screen or page a person uses.

label: Endpoint
description: An HTTP endpoint: its method, route, request and responses.

label: Interaction requirement
description: One rule a view, endpoint or flow must follow, such as a field's limits or an error's response, stated with MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD or MAY.

label: Layer
description: An ordered part of a domain's technical specification that groups its components by what they are, such as Models, Services or Web app. It sits in the domain, or in another layer as a sub-layer. Its order is a whole number giving its place among the layers beside it.

label: Component
description: A unit of code in the target design, such as a model, service or router. It sits in its domain's layer, or in the domain when the domain has no layers.

label: Test
description: A test that proves obligations, or supports them without proving them. Its state is automated (the default; it names the file that runs it in run_by), manual, or planned. An optional `key` is text its file contains in place of IDs, and an optional `key_file` names the file that holds the key, when the test runs from a shared class in another file.

label: Open question
description: Something undecided, with the person who decides it.

label: Fitness
description: How well the product serves its purpose, as judged by the person it serves on a date: a score from 1 to 5 and the experiences behind it.
